candidates.statement: Aluminum content of large volume parenteral (LVP) drug products 5 must not exceed 25 32 micrograms per liter (mcg/L). 6 However, the limits for the aluminum content of SVPs are not 33 specified by statute or regulation. Further, the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) has 34 not established a permitted daily exposure (PDE) for aluminum. 7
candidates.context: 4 The recommendations in this guidance do not apply to the aluminum adjuvants used in vaccines to elicit a stronger immune response. Due to the potential health risks from long-term exposure to aluminum, as explained in the 37 Background section below, FDA aims to have sponsors and applicants limit the individual 38 aluminum exposure (IAE) in each drug product to ensure that the TAE from all components of 39 PN in an admixture (LVPs plus SVPs) does not exceed 4 to 5 micrograms/kilogram/day 40 (mcg/kg/day) of aluminum, a level above which toxicity may occur (as described in 21 CFR 41 201.323(e)). candidates.context: In one controlled trial, 10 preterm neonates were randomized to receive PN with standard 94 aluminum content (mean of 45 mcg/kg/day) or aluminum-depleted PN (mean of 4 to 5 95 mcg/kg/day). Patients treated with standard PN for more than 10 days had lower scores on 96 developmental assessments at 18 months compared with the aluminum-depleted PN group. A 97 follow-up study that evaluated a subset of survivors at age 13 to 15 years showed lower bone 98 mineral content in the lower lumbar spine and hips in the group treated with standard PN. 11 Multiple sources of LVPs and SVPs comprise PN, and each drug product contributes to the total 103 aluminum content of PN. Sponsors and applicants should consider the recommended aluminum 104 limit in an individual SVP because the aluminum limit determines the drug product’s 105 contribution to the total daily aluminum exposure from PN. candidates.statement: The first step in calculating the ACL for the specific SVP is the selection of the IAE. The IAE 127 should be selected to ensure that the addition of the SVP to a PN admixture containing multiple 128 SVPs and LVPs will not cause the TAE to exceed 5 mcg/kg/day. The number of SVP additives 129 will vary for individual patients based on their nutritional needs. A practical approach for 130 ensuring that the addition of SVPs to PN admixtures does not result in TAE values greater than 5 131 mcg/kg/day is to select a single (constant) IAE. Selection and application of the IAE should 132 occur during the early developmental stages of SVPs. 133

candidates.statement: For this approach, the recommended IAE for an individual SVP is 0.6 mcg/kg/day or lower. 152 Selection of 0.6 mcg/kg/day as the constant IAESVP allows for the addition of up to five SVPs 153 with reasonable assurance that the TAE will not exceed 5 mcg/kg/day, based on the expectation 154 that the total aluminum exposure from LVPs (IAELVPtotal) will not exceed 2 mcg/kg/day 155 (aluminum is controlled at 25 mcg/L in LVPs, per 21 CFR 201.323). Further, if use of more than 156 five SVPs in a PN admixture is anticipated, then the selection of an IAESVP should be 157 substantially lower than 0.6 mcg/kg/day to ensure that the TAE will not exceed 5 mcg/kg/day. 158

candidates.statement: Control of elemental impurities to ensure that the levels do not exceed the PDE is one part of the 330 overall control strategy for a drug product. ICH Q3D(R2) provides general recommendations for 331 risk assessment and control of elemental impurities. ICH Q3D(R2) does not provide 332 recommendations of the actual values of the established PDE for some elemental impurities 333 including aluminum for several reasons, including the differences in regulations and practices 334 among geographic regions. Applicants and manufacturers must use validated assay methods to 335 determine the aluminum content in PN. The assay methods must comply with current good 336 manufacturing practice requirements. 16 Sponsors and applicants should establish the appropriate 337 acceptance criterion of the aluminum content in an SVP based on the following two factors: 338

candidates.statement: As part of the risk mitigation, the control of aluminum should be considered in the proposed 375 quality target product profile (e.g., route of administration, patient population, drug product 376 formulation design, strength, primary packaging materials). As illustrated in the SVP ACL 377 calculation formula in section III.B. and examples in section IV.B., the ACL is proportional to 378 the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) concentration for an individual SVP if the maximum 379 daily dose of the SVP and its IAE remains unchanged. Under such a circumstance, a higher 380 aluminum concentration resulting from a higher ACL will be anticipated when an applicant has 381 selected a higher API concentration during the SVP formulation design. FDA encourages the 382 applicant to discuss the aluminum control strategy with FDA’s review divisions when 383 developing SVPs intended to be a component of PN. 17 Finally, the applicant should also 384 implement an adequate control strategy for postapproval changes that could affect aluminum 385 content in the drug product during its life cycle. 386
